newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's NW Prairie likely saw frost, skies clear.
newsitem.headline: Canada's NW Prairie likely saw frost, skies clear.

text.p: Canada's northwest Prairie grainbelt likely saw some frost Monday morning as skies were forecast to continue clearing across the entire region, Environment Canada said.
"There was maybe some patchy frost north of Edmonton towards Slave Lake, between minus one and plus two (at chest level)," meteorologist Mike McDonald told Reuters.
Ground level temperatures can be 2.0 to 5.0 Celsius lower.
Skies were clear in north and central Alberta overnight, he said.
The rest of the Prairies saw lows of 5.0 to 8.0 Celsius.
Alberta was forecast to see continuing clearing skies in the south with highs between 14 and 19 Celsius.
Saskatchewan was forecast to see clearing skies with highs of 14 to 19 Celsius.
Manitoba was forecast to see a mix of sun and cloud with scattered showers and highs around 24 Celsius.
The region's normal high at this time is 20 Celsius.
